evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3538486 was scored at 0.998 by the second-generation fraud model, corresponding to a 92.1% historical fraud rate among transactions at this score tier.

Device D008998 links card C06532-K2 to two other cards, C05116-K1 and C13037-K1, within a 48-hour window; all three cards conducted online purchases of ~$150 for product H with model scores exceeding 0.93, producing a 48.43 fraud lift on this device.

Transaction 3538486 ($149.92) was executed at 03:56:20 on 2016-12-13, just 3 minutes and 20 seconds after transaction 3538480 ($150.05) on card C05116-K1 from the same device D008998, followed 48 hours later by transaction 3544636 for the identical amount of $149.92 on card C13037-K1.

Transaction 3538486 is an online purchase for product H, which sharply deviates from the cardholder's historical baseline of 258 in-person purchases in product category W out of 281 prior transactions.

Device D008998 has a generic desktop profile (Windows 7, Chrome 60.0), was marked as 'Found' rather than 'New' for the account, was not operated behind a proxy, and has no fraud ring association (ring_id -1).
Flagged transaction 3538486 originated in billing region 315, which matches the primary billing region for card C06532-K2 (230 of 281 prior transactions) and carries a low fraud lift of 0.34.
Card C06532-K2 has only one prior closed case, CC-0116, which was cleared as legitimate cardholder travel, with zero prior confirmed fraud cases on the card.
TigerGraph Louvain community detection assigns card C06532-K2 to community 132120586 with zero confirmed fraud cases and a lift of 0.0 vs base rate.

case.summary: Transaction 3538486 for $149.92 on card C06532-K2 was flagged after the bank's fraud model scored it at 0.998 despite a legacy risk score of 0.17. Graph investigation revealed that device D008998 was used to execute near-identical online purchases of approximately $150 in product category H across three distinct cards within 48 hours, including transaction 3538480 on card C05116-K1 just 3 minutes and 20 seconds earlier. This online transaction sharply deviates from the cardholder's baseline of 258 in-person purchases in product category W. Given the synchronized multi-card compromise and calibrated model score, the activity is determined to be unauthorized card-not-present fraud. Card C06532-K2 was blocked, a case created, a regulatory report filed, and linked cards placed on monitoring.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details coordinated card-not-present fraud impacting customer C06532 on card C06532-K2, along with linked cards C05116-K1 and C13037-K1. Between December 13, 2016 and December 15, 2016, an unauthorized party utilized device D008998 (identified as a Windows 7 desktop running Chrome 60.0 with screen resolution 2112x1188) to execute three online transactions in product category H totaling $449.89. The subject transaction 3538486 for $149.92 occurred on card C06532-K2 on December 13, 2016 at 03:56:20 UTC in billing region 315. This transaction was initiated just 3 minutes and 20 seconds after transaction 3538480 ($150.05) was conducted on card C05116-K1 from the identical device. On December 15, 2016, device D008998 was used again to conduct transaction 3544636 for the identical amount of $149.92 on card C13037-K1. All three transactions generated fraud model scores exceeding 0.93, producing an elevated fraud lift of 48.43 on device D008998. The online purchase of product category H sharply deviates from cardholder C06532-K2's baseline of 258 in-person transactions in category W out of 281 historical purchases. Ongoing in-person transactions in region 315 on the same date indicate that the legitimate cardholder remained in possession of the physical card while credentials were compromised. Direct exposure on card C06532-K2 is $149.92, with an aggregate of $449.89 across the three compromised cards. The bank has blocked card C06532-K2 and initiated monitoring on connected cards C05116-K1 and C13037-K1 to mitigate further exposure.

stop_reason: The investigation concluded under policy section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.97, exceeding the decisive threshold of 0.85 supported by multiple independent incriminating findings, making further inquiries unnecessary.
